questions.question: When you park or stop on a grade, you should turn the front wheels:
choices: Straight ahead and rely on the transmission
Away from the curb so the vehicle rolls clear
In whichever direction is easiest to drive out
To the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll
questions.explanation: Turning the front wheels to the curb side of the highway means that if the vehicle creeps, the wheels bring it against the kerb instead of into traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

questions.question: Besides turning the wheels, what else does the handbook require when parking on a grade?
choices: Setting the emergency or parking brake
Leaving the vehicle in neutral
Chocking a wheel
Parking with two wheels on the sidewalk
questions.explanation: You must be sure to set the emergency or parking brake, and the handbook adds that in an automatic you put the selector in park to reinforce it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

questions.subtopic: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
questions.question: When you have finished parallel parking, your wheels should be within how far of the curb?
choices: 24 inches
36 inches
18 inches
12 inches
questions.explanation: The handbook requires the wheels to be parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb, and the vehicle to face the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: When parallel parking on the left side of the road, wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb.  Park in the direction of the traffic.

questions.subtopic: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
questions.question: You have parallel parked on the left side of a one-way street. Which curb do the wheels have to be within 18 inches of?
choices: The right curb
Either curb
Neither — the 18-inch rule only applies on the right
The left curb
questions.explanation: When parallel parking on the left side of the road the wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb, and the vehicle still faces the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: When parallel parking on the left side of the road, wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb.  Park in the direction of the traffic.

questions.question: The handbook's recommended method for judging following distance is:
choices: Two car lengths at any speed
Half the speedometer reading in feet
The three-to-four second rule
One car length for every 10 mph
questions.explanation: The best way to assure proper following distance is the three-to-four second rule, which stays correct at every speed without any arithmetic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The best way to assure proper following distance is to use the three-to-four second rule.

questions.question: The vehicle ahead passes a bridge abutment and you reach it while still saying 'one thousand two'. What does that tell you?
choices: You have a safe gap
You are following too far back
The test only works at low speed
You are following too closely
questions.explanation: If you reach the fixed object before you finish saying 'one thousand three', you are driving too closely and need to drop back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a suitable fixed object for counting following distance?
choices: The vehicle ahead of you
A signpost
An overpass
A bridge abutment
questions.explanation: The object has to be fixed — the handbook names a signpost, tree, overpass or bridge abutment — because a moving vehicle gives you no reference point.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

questions.question: If it is dark or raining, your following distance should be at least:
choices: Four seconds
Two seconds
Three seconds
Six seconds
questions.explanation: The handbook raises the minimum to at least four seconds when it is dark or raining, because both sight and grip are reduced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If it is dark or raining, the distance should be at least four seconds.

questions.question: There is ice and snow on the road. How far back should you stay from the vehicle in front?
choices: The same as in dry conditions
At least six seconds
At least four seconds
At least three seconds
questions.explanation: On ice or snow you should stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front, double the usual dry-weather figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

questions.question: A driver is keeping a six-second gap. Which condition does the handbook match to that distance?
choices: Dry daylight driving
Following a motorcycle in the dry
Ice or snow
Dark or raining
questions.explanation: Six seconds is the figure the handbook gives for ice or snow; four seconds covers dark or rain and three to four is the general baseline.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

questions.question: Besides checking your mirrors, what must you do before changing lanes?
choices: Sound your horn
Flash your headlights
Slow to below the speed limit
Check over your shoulder for the blind spot
questions.explanation: A head check over the left or right shoulder is needed because mirrors do not cover the blind spot where another vehicle can sit unseen.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

questions.question: Where does the handbook say you must NOT change lanes?
choices: In an intersection or at a railroad crossing
On a four-lane divided highway
Within 100 feet of a driveway
Anywhere broken white lines are present
questions.explanation: The rule is DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing, both places where vehicles enter your path from directions you are not watching.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

questions.question: You have checked your mirrors and your blind spot and both are clear. What is the remaining check the handbook lists?
choices: Whether you are exceeding the minimum speed
Whether another driver is also moving into the same lane
Whether your tyres are correctly inflated
Whether the lane ends within a mile
questions.explanation: The handbook adds a check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane — the vehicle converging from the far side that neither mirror nor head check covers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears their front bumper
After counting five seconds
When the passed driver flashes their lights
When you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror
questions.explanation: Seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear view mirror is the handbook's proof that you have left it enough space to keep braking distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

questions.question: Passing on the right is:
choices: Not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing
Always permissible on a multi-lane road
Permissible if the vehicle ahead is turning left
Permissible at any intersection
questions.explanation: The handbook says passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

questions.question: You are about to overtake on a two-lane highway at night. What does the handbook allow you to do to alert the driver ahead?
choices: Sound a long horn blast only
Blink your headlights
Flash your hazard lights
Use your high beams continuously
questions.explanation: You should sound your horn to alert the driver ahead, and at night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Move left when clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing. At night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

questions.subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
questions.question: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection?
choices: 200 feet
500 feet
100 feet
50 feet
questions.explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of an intersection, because a vehicle can emerge into the lane you are occupying.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: On a curve or hill or at any place where you cannot see oncoming traffic.

questions.subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a place where the handbook prohibits passing?
choices: Within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass
On a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic
When the solid yellow line is in your lane
On a straight, level road with a broken yellow line on your side
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side of a clear, straight road is exactly where passing is allowed when it is safe; the other three are on the prohibited list.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: Within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, or underpass.

questions.subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
questions.question: The car ahead of you has stopped at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross. May you pass it?
choices: No — passing is prohibited in that situation
Yes, if you pass on the right
Yes, if the pedestrian has passed your lane
Yes, if no oncoming traffic is visible
questions.explanation: Passing is prohibited when a vehicle in front of you has stopped at an intersection to allow a pedestrian to cross, because the stopped car hides the pedestrian from you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: When a vehicle in front of you has stopped at an intersection to allow a pedestrian to cross.

questions.question: You are following a slow vehicle and considering a pass. Which condition must be satisfied first?
choices: The vehicle ahead signals you to go
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic
You can complete the pass within 100 feet
You can reach at least 10 mph above the limit
questions.explanation: The handbook states you cannot pass safely unless you can see far enough ahead, can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed needed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.

questions.question: The handbook describes right-of-way as something that is:
choices: Assigned by vehicle size
Held by the faster vehicle
Given, not taken
Earned by arriving first
questions.explanation: Right-of-way is something to be given rather than taken, and if another driver does not follow the rules you are told to give it to them anyway.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, in every situation, right-of-way is something to be given, not taken.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way at an intersection, but another driver pulls out in front of you anyway. What does the handbook expect?
choices: Hold your course, since the rules are on your side
Sound the horn and continue at the same speed
Accelerate to clear the intersection first
Give the right-of-way rather than insist on it
questions.explanation: The handbook is explicit that if the other driver does not follow the rules, you give the right-of-way; being right is no protection in a collision.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, in every situation, right-of-way is something to be given, not taken.

questions.question: When entering a public street from an alley, private road or driveway you must:
choices: Stop only if a sign requires it
Yield to traffic already on the roadway
Proceed, because entering traffic has priority
Yield only to vehicles approaching from the left
questions.explanation: Traffic already on the roadway has the right-of-way over a vehicle entering it from an alley, private road or driveway.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When entering a public street or highway from an alley, private road, or driveway, you must yield to traffic already on the roadway.

questions.question: You are leaving a shop car park across a sidewalk and onto a busy street. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You, because the car park exit is signed
Whoever arrives at the kerb line first
Pedestrians on the sidewalk and traffic already on the street
You, because you are already in motion
questions.explanation: You must yield to traffic already on the roadway, and pedestrians have the right of way where the sidewalk crosses a driveway entrance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: They are crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time. Who goes first?
choices: The driver on the left
The vehicle going straight ahead
The larger vehicle
The driver on the right
questions.explanation: At uncontrolled intersections and four-way stops, a driver who arrives at the same time as another vehicle yields to the driver on the right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Uncontrolled intersections and four-way stop intersections - If you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals at the same moment as a car to your right. What must you do?
choices: Yield to the car on your right
Proceed, since there are no signs
Yield only if it is turning
Sound your horn and proceed
questions.explanation: The same-time rule covers uncontrolled intersections as well as four-way stops: yield to the driver on the right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Uncontrolled intersections and four-way stop intersections - If you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection controlled by a yield sign. What does the handbook require before the intersection?
choices: Yield only to traffic already inside the intersection
Slow down before reaching it, then yield to vehicles in it and to approaching traffic
Stop completely at the sign every time
Maintain speed unless a vehicle is visible
questions.explanation: At intersections with yield signs you slow down before reaching the intersection, then yield to any vehicle in the intersection and to approaching traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Intersections with yield signs - Slow down before reaching the intersection

questions.question: When making a left turn you must yield the right-of-way to:
choices: Traffic on the cross street only
No one, if you signalled
Oncoming traffic
Traffic behind you
questions.explanation: A left turn crosses the path of oncoming traffic, which is why the turning driver must always yield to it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When making a left turn, you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are turning left and an oncoming vehicle is about to reach the intersection at roughly the same time as you. What should you do?
choices: Turn quickly ahead of it
Turn while sounding your horn
Proceed, since you arrived at the intersection first
Stop until it is safe for you to turn
questions.explanation: The handbook says that if traffic is about to reach the intersection at approximately the same time, stop until it is safe for you to turn.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When turning left, watch for approaching traffi  c in the opposite lane.

questions.question: An ambulance approaches with siren sounding and lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop
Stop immediately wherever you are, including in the intersection
Speed up to clear the road ahead
Move to the left edge of the road
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights by pulling to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stopping until it passes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: You must yield to any emergency vehicle (ambulance, fire, or police vehicle) that is sounding a siren and flashing warning lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: You have pulled over and stopped for a fire engine. What two things does the handbook tell you to do next?
choices: Move off as soon as its lights are out of sight
Keep your foot on the brake, and watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding
Switch off your engine and wait two minutes
Follow the fire engine to clear the traffic
questions.explanation: Keeping your foot on the brake shows the emergency driver you are stopped, and you should watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding because they often travel in groups.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Keep your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped. Watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic and waves you through a red light. What controls?
choices: The red signal, which always controls
Whichever came first
The road markings
The officer's direction, which overrules any sign, signal or road marking
questions.explanation: Directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal or road marking.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal, or road marking.

questions.question: Which statement about funeral processions is NOT correct?
choices: The law requires you to yield to a funeral procession
Yielding to a procession is a courtesy
Once the lead vehicle has cleared an intersection the rest of the procession has the right-of-way
You may pass a procession on an expressway
questions.explanation: Yielding to a funeral procession is a courtesy rather than a legal requirement, though the procession does hold the right-of-way once its lead vehicle has cleared the intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Although not required by law, it is a courtesy to yield to vehicles in a funeral procession.

questions.question: Pedestrians have the right of way when they are:
choices: Only at signalised intersections
Only in school zones
In a crosswalk
Anywhere on the roadway at any time
questions.explanation: The handbook lists a crosswalk first among the places pedestrians have the right of way, along with a sidewalk crossing an alley or driveway and a blind person crossing with a cane or guide dog.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, pedestrians have the right of way when:

questions.question: A person is walking along the sidewalk and is about to cross the mouth of the driveway you are pulling out of. Who has the right of way?
choices: You, because the driveway is private
Whoever moves first
The pedestrian only if the driveway is marked
The pedestrian
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right of way when crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway, which is exactly this situation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: They are crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway.

questions.question: Why does the handbook demand extreme care near school zones, bus stops, playgrounds and parks?
choices: Vehicle-pedestrian collisions account for nearly 20% of traffic fatalities and those are places pedestrians gather
Speed limits are unmarked there
Pedestrians never have the right of way there
Parking is prohibited there
questions.explanation: Nearly a fifth of traffic fatalities involve pedestrians, and the handbook names school zones, bus stops, playgrounds and parks as places where special hazards exist.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Vehicle-pedestrian collisions account for nearly 20% of traffic  fatalities. Drivers must use extreme care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian, especially in areas where special hazards exist, such as school zones, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Pedestrians - Pedestrians must
questions.question: Where there is no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk:
choices: On the left side, facing oncoming traffic
On the right side, with traffic
In the centre of the lane
Only after dark with a light
questions.explanation: Walking on the left facing oncoming traffic lets a pedestrian see an approaching vehicle and step clear, which walking with traffic does not.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Pedestrians - Pedestrians must
source.sourceQuote: When walking along a road where there is no sidewalk, walk on the left side facing oncoming traffic. Walk on the shoulder of the road, if possible.

questions.question: Which of these may a pedestrian NOT do?
choices: Obey WALK and DON'T WALK signals
Walk on an interstate highway
Use crosswalks at intersections
Walk on the shoulder where there is no sidewalk
questions.explanation: Pedestrians must not walk on interstate highways or other areas where signs to that effect are posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Pedestrians must not walk on interstate highways or other areas where signs to that effect are posted.

questions.question: A school bus ahead stops with its red lights flashing to let children off. Which traffic must stop?
choices: Only traffic behind the bus
Only traffic in the same lane as the bus
Only traffic on undivided streets
Traffic in both directions
questions.explanation: On all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus with its red lights flashing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

choices: Yes — the rule covers parking lots, private roads and driveways as well as highways
No, because it is not a public highway
No, because car parks have no lane markings
Only if children are visible outside the bus
questions.explanation: The rule expressly covers all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways, so a car park is included.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

choices: The bus must have its red lights flashing
You only have to stop on public highways
The rule covers parking lots, private roads and driveways as well as highways
Traffic in both directions must stop
questions.explanation: The obligation is not limited to public highways: the rule expressly names all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus, when may you proceed?
choices: When the bus resumes motion, the driver signals you on, or the visual signals stop
As soon as the last child leaves the roadway
After waiting ten seconds
As soon as the door closes
questions.explanation: You may not proceed until the bus resumes motion, you are signalled by the school bus driver, or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: The children have left the bus and walked away, but the red lights are still flashing. May you go?
choices: Yes, if you are travelling in the opposite direction
No — the visual signals are still actuated
Yes, because the children are clear
Yes, if you pass slowly
questions.explanation: Until the bus moves off, the driver signals you, or the visual signals stop operating, you must remain stopped — another child may still be crossing.

source.sourceQuote: proceed until the bus resumes motion, or signaled by the school bus driver to proceed or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

questions.question: On which type of road does traffic coming toward a stopped school bus on the other side of a median NOT have to stop?
choices: Any four-lane road
Roads with a posted limit of 55 mph or more
Interstate highways
Any divided highway
questions.explanation: The handbook gives exactly one exception: only on interstate highways does traffic coming toward a bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Only on Interstate Highways does traffic coming toward a school bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

questions.question: You are on a divided four-lane road that is not an interstate when a school bus on the other side of the median stops with red lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Continue, because the median separates you
Slow to 15 mph and continue
Continue only if no children are visible
Stop, because the exception applies only to interstate highways
questions.explanation: The exception is limited to interstate highways, so on any other divided road oncoming traffic must still stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Only on Interstate Highways does traffic coming toward a school bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

questions.question: What is the minimum driver's license suspension for a first offence of passing a stopped school bus?
choices: 60 days
30 days
90 days
Six months
questions.explanation: A first offence carries a minimum 60-day driver's license suspension, together with a minimum $500 fine or confinement in jail for not more than six months.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The penalty for passing a stopped school bus is a minimum of 60 days driver’s license suspension and a minimum fine of $500 or confinement in jail for not more than six (6) months for the first offense.

questions.question: Which statement about the penalty for passing a stopped school bus is NOT correct?
choices: If the driver cannot be identified, the owner or lessee may be guilty of a misdemeanor
Subsequent offences carry the same penalty as the first
The minimum fine for a first offence is $500
The minimum licence suspension for a first offence is 60 days
questions.explanation: The handbook states that subsequent offences have increased penalties, so they are not treated the same as a first offence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The penalty for passing a stopped school bus is a minimum of 60 days driver’s license suspension and a minimum fine of $500 or confinement in jail for not more than six (6) months for the first offense.

questions.question: You must dim your headlights within how many feet of an approaching vehicle?
choices: 500 feet
200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: High beams must be dimmed within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle so you do not blind the oncoming driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Dim your headlights within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle.

questions.question: You must dim your headlights within how many feet of the vehicle in front of you?
choices: 300 feet
200 feet
500 feet
100 feet
questions.explanation: Following another vehicle, dim within 200 feet, because your high beams reflect off their mirrors into their eyes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Dim your headlights within 200 feet of the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: A vehicle is approaching with its high beams on and you are dazzled. What does the handbook say to do?
choices: Close one eye until it passes
Brake hard and stop
Look toward the right edge of the road instead of at the lights
Switch your own high beams on to match
questions.explanation: Avoid looking directly into the lights of oncoming vehicles by looking toward the right edge of the road, which keeps you on course while your eyes recover.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Avoid looking directly into the lights of oncoming vehicles by looking toward the right edge of the road.

questions.question: Headlights must be turned on:
choices: From sunset to sunrise, and whenever people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 500 feet
Only between midnight and dawn
Only when it is fully dark
Only when other drivers flash you
questions.explanation: The rule covers sunset to sunrise plus fog, smoke or rain, and any other time people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at a distance of 500 feet.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Turn on your headlights from sunset to sunrise, during fog, smoke, rain, or at any other time when persons and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at a distance of 500 feet.

questions.question: You are driving into thick fog in the middle of the afternoon. Which lights should you use?
choices: Hazard lights only
Low beams
High beams
Parking lights
questions.explanation: Use low beam lights when driving in fog, because high beams cause the light to be reflected back into your eyes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Use low beam lights when driving in fog. High beams cause the light to be reflected back into your eyes.

questions.question: Which of these uses of lights is NOT correct?
choices: Turning headlights on during smoke or rain
Keeping headlights and taillights properly adjusted and cleaned
Driving on parking lights in light rain
Using low beams in fog
questions.explanation: Parking lights are to be used only when you are parked; rain calls for headlights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Use your parking lights only when you are parked.

questions.question: A vehicle is following you too closely. What is the first step the handbook gives?
choices: Tap your brakes gently to flash the brake lights
Accelerate to open the gap
Brake hard to warn them
Move into the left lane
questions.explanation: Tapping the brakes gently flashes the brake lights and warns the tailgater without the risk of a hard brake application in front of them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Tap your brakes gently to flash the brake lights and warn the tailgater.

questions.question: Flashing your brake lights has not worked and the driver is still tailgating you. What should you do next?
choices: Straddle the lane line to block them
Slow down to encourage them to pass, and if that fails pull over and let them by
Speed up until they fall behind
Brake hard to force them back
questions.explanation: The handbook's sequence is to slow down to encourage the vehicle to pass, and if all else fails, pull over, stop and let it pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If all else fails, pull over, stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.question: How much of a lane is a motorcyclist entitled to?
choices: The entire lane
Half the lane
Only the right-hand portion
Only as much as the rider is using at that moment
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to manoeuvre around hazards and traffic situations, so you must never share a lane with one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

questions.question: The motorcyclist ahead of you moves from one side of the lane to the other. What should you conclude?
choices: The rider has lost control
This is normal — riders move around in the lane to handle hazards
The rider is inviting you to pass in the same lane
The rider is about to turn
questions.explanation: Motorists should expect to see motorcyclists move around in their lane, because the rider needs the whole width to avoid road hazards.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

questions.question: What minimum following distance does the handbook suggest behind a motorcycle?
choices: One second, since motorcycles are short
Six seconds at all times
Three to four seconds, increased at night and in bad weather
Two seconds in all conditions
questions.explanation: It is wise to keep a safe minimum three-to-four second following distance behind a motorcycle and to increase it at night and under adverse weather conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle you should:
choices: Stay in your lane and use the left half
Go all the way into the other lane
Share the lane and pass alongside
Pass on the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Go all the way into the other lane: besides having the legal right to an entire lane, the rider may need to swerve to avoid something on the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Stay farther back than if you were behind a vehicle.  The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can.  When passing, go all the way into the other lane.

questions.question: Why does the handbook tell you to stay farther back behind a motorcycle than behind a car?
choices: Motorcycles have no brake lights
Motorcycles are required to stop at every intersection
The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can
Motorcycles accelerate more slowly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than the vehicle behind it, so the normal car-following gap is not enough.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Stay farther back than if you were behind a vehicle.  The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can.  When passing, go all the way into the other lane.

questions.question: You have just overtaken a motorcycle. When should you move back?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears it
Immediately, to reduce time in the other lane
When the rider flashes their headlight
Once you are well down the road
questions.explanation: Once you have passed, wait until you are well down the road before moving back into the other lane, so you do not cut into the rider's braking space.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Once you have passed, wait until you are well down the road before moving back into the other lane.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer travelling 55 mph needs how much distance to stop compared with a car?
choices: Half again as much
Twice the distance
Three times the distance
The same distance
questions.explanation: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs three times the distance a car needs to stop, which is why the space in front of one is not yours to take.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
source.sourceQuote: A fully loaded tractor-trailer, traveling 55 mph, needs three (3) times the distance a vehicle needs to stop.

questions.question: Your exit is approaching and you have just passed a loaded truck. What is the risk in cutting straight back in front of it?
choices: The truck cannot change lanes
You may damage the truck's mirrors
The truck will be unable to signal
You take away the distance the truck needs to stop
questions.explanation: A loaded truck needs three times a car's stopping distance, so moving into that space leaves it no room to stop if traffic slows; the handbook says never to cut off a truck to reach your exit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Never cut off a truck in traffic or on the highway to reach your exit or turn.

questions.question: The No-Zone around a heavy truck refers to:
choices: The area directly in front of the truck's bumper only
A lane reserved for trucks
The distance a truck needs to turn
The truck's blind spots, where the driver cannot see you
questions.explanation: The No-Zone is the truck's blind spots, which are dangerous because truck drivers cannot see vehicles in those areas.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The easiest way to avoid lingering in the “No-Zone” is to look for the truck driver’s reflection in the side mirror. If you cannot see the driver’s reflection, you are in the truck driver’s blind spot.

questions.question: How can you tell whether you are in a truck's blind spot?
choices: If you cannot see the driver's reflection in the side mirror
If you cannot see the truck's rear doors
If the truck's headlights are not visible
If you are within two car lengths
questions.explanation: The easiest test is to look for the truck driver's reflection in the side mirror: if you cannot see the driver's reflection, you are in the blind spot.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The easiest way to avoid lingering in the “No-Zone” is to look for the truck driver’s reflection in the side mirror. If you cannot see the driver’s reflection, you are in the truck driver’s blind spot.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
questions.question: Which statement about heavy trucks is NOT correct?
choices: Heavy trucks typically weigh 80,000 pounds
Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars because the driver sits higher
Trucks are longer, heavier and need more room to turn
Trucks have larger blind spots than vehicles
questions.explanation: Trucks have larger blind spots than cars, and typically the larger the vehicle the larger the blind spots.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
source.sourceQuote: Trucks have larger blind spots than vehicles.

questions.question: After passing a truck in dry conditions, how much space should you allow before merging back to the right?
choices: Four seconds
Six seconds
Two seconds
One second
questions.explanation: In dry conditions use the two-second rule and give two seconds before merging to the right after passing a truck.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: In dry conditions use the two-second rule. After passing give two (2) seconds before merging to the right.

questions.question: The road is wet and you have just passed a tractor-trailer. How much space should you leave before moving back over?
choices: Two seconds, as in the dry
One second
Ten seconds
At least four to six seconds
questions.explanation: In wet conditions the handbook calls for at least four to six seconds of space, because the truck's stopping distance grows on a wet surface.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: In wet conditions give at least  four (4) to six (6) seconds of space.

questions.question: Which of these does the handbook list under things you should NEVER do around a truck?
choices: Pass a truck on the right during a turn
Give a truck extra room for right turns
Give trucks extra space and time for backing up
Call authorities if you see unsafe truck driving
questions.explanation: Never pass a truck on the right during a turn — a truck swinging wide to turn right will close on anything beside it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Never pass a truck on the right during a turn.

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist you should:
choices: Pass close so you stay in your own lane
Slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room
Pass quickly to minimise the time alongside
Sound your horn continuously while alongside
questions.explanation: Slowing, making sure the rider knows you are there and leaving plenty of room is the handbook's instruction for passing a bicyclist.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When passing a bicyclist, slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room between him or her and your vehicle.  If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing.

questions.question: There is no room to pass a bicyclist safely and a car is approaching from the other direction. What should you do?
choices: Sound your horn so the cyclist moves over
Pass on the shoulder
Wait until the oncoming traffic has gone by before passing
Squeeze past while staying in your lane
questions.explanation: If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing — the room the rider needs does not shrink because you are in a hurry.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When passing a bicyclist, slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room between him or her and your vehicle.  If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing.

questions.question: Bicyclists on the road must:
choices: Yield to all motor vehicles at all times
Ride only on the shoulder
Obey the same rules of the road as drivers of other vehicles
Ride facing oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: Bicyclists are expected to know and obey all traffic laws and regulations, the same rules of the road as drivers of other vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Obey the same rules of the road as drivers of other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a duty the handbook places on bicyclists?
choices: Riding in the same direction as other vehicles
Yielding the right-of-way to pedestrians
Signalling turns and stops unless both hands are needed for balance
Riding facing oncoming traffic so they can see it
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as other vehicles; walking facing traffic is the rule for pedestrians, not for cyclists.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Ride in the same direction as other vehicles.

questions.question: A bicyclist ahead of you is riding in a way that looks unlawful. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Give them the benefit of the doubt whether they are operating lawfully or not
Sound your horn to correct them
Pass closely to discourage them
Follow closely until they move aside
questions.explanation: Whether the bicyclist is operating lawfully or not, the handbook tells drivers to always give him or her the benefit of the doubt, because almost any collision injures the rider.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: However, whether the bicyclist is operating lawfully or not, always give him or her the benefit of the doubt.

questions.question: A bicycle bell or other warning device must be audible for a distance of at least:
choices: 100 feet
50 feet
200 feet
500 feet
questions.explanation: Required equipment includes a bell or other device capable of giving a signal audible for at least 100 feet, though no siren or whistle is permitted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Bell or other device capable of giving a signal audible for a distance of at least 100 feet

questions.question: A bicycle ridden after dark must carry a white headlight visible for at least how far to the front?
choices: 300 feet
500 feet
100 feet
200 feet
questions.explanation: For riding after dark a bicycle needs a white headlight visible for at least 500 feet to the front, along with a red reflector on the rear.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: For riding after dark, a white headlight that is visible for at least  500 feet to the front.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required equipment on a bicycle?
choices: Brakes able to stop one wheel on dry, level, clean pavement
A bell audible for at least 100 feet
A siren
A red reflector on the rear
questions.explanation: A bell or other audible device is required but the handbook expressly says no siren or whistle is permitted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Bell or other device capable of giving a signal audible for a distance of at least 100 feet

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
questions.question: When you approach a horse and rider on the road you must never:
choices: Sound your horn
Slow down
Move over to give room
Dim your headlights
questions.explanation: Never sound your horn when approaching or near a horse, as this may frighten the horse and cause a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
source.sourceQuote: Never sound your horn when approaching or near a horse, as this may frighten the horse and cause a crash.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
questions.question: Where may a person riding an animal not go?
choices: Business districts
Interstate highways
Any paved public highway
Roads with a centre line
questions.explanation: Animal riders may use most public highways but they may not use interstate highways.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
source.sourceQuote: Animal riders may use most public highways, but they may not use interstate highways.  Persons riding animals have the same rights as  motor vehicle users and are subject to the same rules.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
questions.question: What rights and duties does a person riding an animal on a public highway have?
choices: Priority over all motor traffic
None, unless the road is unpaved
The same rights as motor vehicle users, and they are subject to the same rules
Fewer rights, since an animal is not a vehicle
questions.explanation: Persons riding animals have the same rights as motor vehicle users and are subject to the same rules of the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Animal Riders
source.sourceQuote: Animal riders may use most public highways, but they may not use interstate highways.  Persons riding animals have the same rights as  motor vehicle users and are subject to the same rules.

questions.subtopic: Sharing the Road with Public Buses
questions.question: Must traffic stop for a public bus that is loading or unloading passengers?
choices: No, but you must watch for passengers crossing the street
Yes, in both directions, as with a school bus
Yes, but only traffic behind the bus
Only if the bus has flashing lights
questions.explanation: Traffic does not have to stop for a public bus, but you must watch for passengers crossing the street as they get on and off, and use caution when passing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Public Buses
source.sourceQuote: While traffic does not have to stop for a public bus, please watch for passengers crossing the street as they are getting on and off the bus.

questions.question: You are driving through a residential street in the late afternoon. What does the handbook ask of you?
choices: Drive in the centre of the road for a better view
Be extra careful, because it is a place and time where children are likely to be around
Maintain the speed limit exactly to keep traffic flowing
Use your horn regularly to warn children
questions.explanation: Drivers are told to be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and at times and places where children are likely to be around.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: As a driver, be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and at times and places where children are likely to be around.

signs.name: Stop sign
signs.meaning: An eight-sided sign reserved for stop signs.
signs.action: Stop completely, then give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all cross traffic before moving again.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These eight-sided signs are reserved for stop signs.  These signs mean you must stop completely. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffi  c before moving again.

signs.name: Yield sign
signs.meaning: A downward-pointing triangle telling you that other traffic has the right-of-way.
signs.action: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic before you proceed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.section: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (upside down)
source.sourceQuote: This shape requires that you yield the right-of-way to cross traffi  c or to merging traffi  c.

signs.name: No-passing zone pennant
signs.meaning: A pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road marking the start of a no-passing zone.
signs.action: Do not begin to pass from this point until the no-passing zone ends.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: This sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.

signs.name: Railroad advance warning
signs.meaning: A round yellow-and-black sign giving advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead.
signs.action: Slow down, look and listen for a train, and be ready to stop before the tracks.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: This yellow-and-black sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead.

signs.name: School zone / school crossing
signs.meaning: A five-sided sign warning of a school zone ahead or marking a school crossing.
signs.action: Slow to the 15 m.p.h. school zone limit when children are present or when specified, and watch for children.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: The maximum speed limit in a school zone is 15 m.p.h. when children are present or when specifi ed.

signs.name: Speed limit sign
signs.meaning: A white rectangular regulatory sign showing the fastest speed allowed under optimal weather and road conditions.
signs.action: Do not exceed the posted number, and drive slower whenever conditions are less than ideal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These signs show the fastest speed you may drive under

signs.name: General warning sign
signs.meaning: A yellow diamond with black symbols or letters warning of possible danger ahead.
signs.action: Slow down, read the symbol and be ready for the hazard it shows.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: These  diamond-shaped signs will usually appear without  explanatory words beneath them.  These signs are yellow with black letters.  They warn of possible danger ahead and may have symbols or written warnings.

signs.name: Pedestrian crossing warning
signs.meaning: A pedestrian or school warning sign, which may be yellow-green with black letters.
signs.action: Slow down and watch for, and yield to, people walking across the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Pedestrian and school warning signs may be yellow-green with black letters.

signs.name: Construction and maintenance sign
signs.meaning: An orange diamond notifying drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near a work area.
signs.action: Slow down, expect workers, equipment and lane shifts, and follow the channelling devices.

signs.name: Railroad crossbuck
signs.meaning: Black letters on white bars in the shape of an X, marking the railroad crossing itself.
signs.action: Yield to all trains, and never enter the crossing unless you can clear the tracks completely.

source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Railroad crossing signs can be round or diamond shaped, yellow with black symbols, or  black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck.

signs.name: Guide sign
signs.meaning: A white-on-green sign telling you where you are, what road you are on and how to get where you are going.
signs.action: Read it early and change lanes in good time for your exit or turn.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Control Devices
source.sourceQuote: Most guide signs are white on green. Motorist services signs are white on blue.   Signs for parks and public recreation areas are white on brown.

signs.name: Motorist services sign
signs.meaning: A white-on-blue sign showing what amenities are available off the exit.
signs.action: Use it to plan fuel, food and rest stops rather than making a late decision at the ramp.
